headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or write capabilities are documented, but marker’s document-processing role could still mis-handle game outputs if manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and marker, and neither profile shows MCP, filesystem sharing, or clipboard bridging. With agent_a network_egress none and agent_b no read/write surfaces, there is no plausible default injection path.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Do not paste agent_a output into agent_b as instructions.
Use a fixed-format handoff template that strips imperative text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no data classes touched, no filesystem read/write, and no network egress. That makes cross-agent leakage of sensitive content via default operation implausible; there is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal to leak through.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and either agent is given file access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of both agents.
Run each agent under separate OS users.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents is a game-playing package with no write or network permissions shown, while marker explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no capability conflict in the documented defaults.
conditions: IF agent_a is wrapped with additional write or git permissions outside the profile, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only in the orchestrator.
Do not grant agent_b filesystem or git write permissions.
Serialize any shared state updates through one controller.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent, so it could consume outputs from godot_rl_agents if an operator manually chains them. However, no default handoff, action-taking authority, or verification bypass is documented, so the cascade is limited to an unusual workflow rather than the pair itself.
conditions: IF an operator feeds agent_a outputs directly into agent_b without review, cascading errors become possible.
mitigations: Use a schema for agent_a outputs and validate it before passing onward.
Reject free-form instructions in the handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either godot_rl_agents or marker, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. With no compliance-sensitive data flow identified, there is no documented compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later used on regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Block regulated data until a policy review is complete.
Record retention and residency settings in the runbook.
